Real-world p-tau217 testing reshapes diagnostic pathways

Across 1,368 consecutive patients at 24 centers, routine plasma p-tau217 testing produced a 19.9% equivocal zone and was associated with fewer CSF requests and reported reductions in diagnostic delay, but the observational design does not establish patient-outcome benefit.

Key quantitative results: Plasma p-tau217 was positive in 66.1% of 997 patients with suspected Alzheimer disease versus 17.8% of 180 with suspected non-Alzheimer conditions; 191 patients had no specific etiologic hypothesis.

BiomarkersBloodp-tau217CSF p-tau181/Aβ42Diagnostic workup

Added October 28, 2026 · DOI:10.1186/s13195-026-02244-9

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

This large real-world series shows what a three-zone p-tau217 pathway looks like after implementation: one in five results remained equivocal, age and renal function affected interpretation, and paired CSF concordance was good rather than perfect. Clinicians reported shorter delays and less FDG-PET use, while CSF requests fell. Those pathway changes are associations, not randomized evidence of clinical utility.

Study design

The investigators analyzed 1,368 consecutive patients tested during routine cognitive-disorder evaluation at 24 secondary or tertiary centers from January through December 2025. Clinical hypotheses were recorded before testing. A retrospective paired-CSF subset included 117 patients; implementation outcomes combined a 53-prescriber survey with laboratory activity data.

Key quantitative results

  • Plasma p-tau217 was positive in 66.1% of 997 patients with suspected Alzheimer disease versus 17.8% of 180 with suspected non-Alzheimer conditions; 191 patients had no specific etiologic hypothesis.
  • Equivocal results occurred in 19.9% and were more common with older age. Concentrations increased with age, were higher in women, and were inversely associated with MMSE and renal function.
  • Among 117 patients with paired testing, plasma p-tau217 correlated with the CSF p-tau181/Aβ42 ratio (Spearman ρ=0.640) and discriminated a positive CSF ratio above 0.10 with AUC 0.870.
  • Of 53 prescribers, 71% reported greater diagnostic confidence, 80% shorter diagnostic delay, and 63% less FDG-PET use after implementation.
  • CSF biomarker requests fell approximately 46% between January–June 2024 and July–December 2025; the uncontrolled before-and-after comparison cannot attribute the reduction solely to p-tau217 testing.

What changed

The study adds large, multicenter operational evidence on equivocal-result burden, patient-level modifiers, CSF concordance, and downstream testing after plasma p-tau217 enters routine specialty care.

Strength of evidence

Moderate implementation evidence from a large consecutive multicenter cohort with objective activity data and a paired-CSF subset. Clinical-utility certainty is limited by the observational design, lack of randomized comparison, self-reported prescriber effects, changing practice over time, and absence of patient outcomes.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

A positive or negative p-tau217 result can streamline a specialty workup, but nearly one in five patients remained equivocal and age, renal function, clinical phenotype, and pretest probability still matter. Discordant or equivocal cases may still require CSF or PET confirmation.

Field medical relevance

Directly informs real-world blood-biomarker interpretation, gray-zone planning, blood-CSF concordance, reflex testing, FDG-PET use, laboratory implementation, and expectations for resource substitution.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The study evaluates a laboratory p-tau217 pathway with predefined low, equivocal, and high categories. Its implementation estimates are setting-specific and should not be transferred to another assay, cutoff system, or prevalence context without validation.

Access or reimbursement relevance

The observed reduction in invasive CSF testing and reported FDG-PET use suggests potential access and workflow benefits, but no formal availability, reimbursement, or coverage change occurred.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does the fall in CSF testing prove clinical utility?
No. It documents a pathway change, but the before-and-after design cannot isolate the effect of p-tau217 or show improved patient outcomes.
Can plasma p-tau217 replace CSF or PET in every patient?
No. The equivocal rate was 19.9%, paired-CSF agreement was not perfect, and patient-specific factors affected concentrations.
What should be integrated with the result?
Clinical phenotype, pretest probability, age, renal function, cognition, and the assay-specific cutoff framework.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Observational implementation design
  • No randomized comparator or patient-outcome endpoint
  • Prescriber survey susceptible to response and recall bias
  • Only 117 patients had paired CSF data
  • Activity comparison spans changing calendar periods
  • Cutoffs and workflow may not generalize across assays or health systems

Primary source · DOI

Bayart JL, Colmant L, Boyer E, et al. Plasma p-tau217 in real-world clinical practice: distribution across clinical diagnostic categories, clinician confidence, and impact on care pathways. Alzheimers Res Ther. Published online October 27, 2026. doi:10.1186/s13195-026-02244-9.
